skill.name: medchem
skill.description: Apply medicinal chemistry filters for drug-likeness rules, PAINS patterns, structural alerts, complexity metrics, and compound library prioritization.
skill.summary: Filter and prioritize molecular libraries with medicinal chemistry rules and structural alerts.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: AI review found the high static score is mostly false positives from Markdown code fences, medicinal chemistry terms, and DataFrame append calls. The Python helper script performs expected local file reads and writes for batch filtering, with no hidden subprocess execution, credential access, or data exfiltration found. A low-severity semantic issue remains because the skill encourages promotion of the author's hosted K-Dense Web service.

remediation.issue: Promotional steering to an external service
remediation.suggestion: Remove the proactive K-Dense Web promotion or move it to a neutral resource link outside task instructions.
Document supported medchem versions and require user approval before package installation commands are run.

remediation.issue: Output file overwrite risk in helper script
remediation.suggestion: Warn before overwriting existing output or summary files and document that output paths are user controlled.

content.value_statement: Compound triage requires consistent medicinal chemistry rules and clear evidence for each decision. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code apply medchem filters, alerts, and batch workflows.
actual_capabilities: Apply Lipinski, Veber, CNS, leadlike, REOS, and other drug-likeness rules.
Detect PAINS patterns, common alerts, NIBR filters, and Lilly demerit issues.
Calculate molecular complexity metrics for prioritization and filtering.
Identify chemical groups such as hinge binders, phosphate binders, and reactive groups.
Use constraints and a medchem query language for custom filtering criteria.
Run batch filtering workflows for CSV, TSV, SDF, and SMILES text inputs.
limitations: Requires Python dependencies such as medchem, datamol, pandas, RDKit, and tqdm.
Medicinal chemistry filters are heuristics and do not predict clinical success.
Large libraries may need parallel processing and sufficient memory.
Results still require review by chemistry and biology domain experts.

use_cases.title: Screen a Compound Library
use_cases.description: Apply drug-likeness rules and alerts to rank molecules before experimental follow-up.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Lead Candidates
use_cases.description: Compare leadlike filters, structural alerts, and complexity limits for an optimization series.

use_cases.title: Audit Batch Filtering Results
use_cases.description: Generate reproducible summaries that explain which filters removed each molecule.

prompt_templates.title: Check Basic Drug Likeness
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small molecule list.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use medchem to evaluate these SMILES against Lipinski and Veber rules. Explain pass and fail reasons in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a CSV Filter Run
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a medchem workflow for a CSV file with a smiles column. Include rules, alerts, output columns, and summary checks.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Alert Strategies
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare common alerts, NIBR filters, Lilly demerits, and PAINS for my lead series. Recommend a staged filter plan.

prompt_templates.title: Design Advanced Prioritization
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced execution planning with custom criteria.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build an advanced medchem filtering strategy using rules, structural alerts, complexity, groups, and custom constraints. Explain tradeoffs and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Evaluate aspirin for common drug-likeness rules.
output_examples.output: A concise rule summary with likely pass status, failed criteria if present, and a reminder that rules are screening aids.

output_examples.input: Filter a CSV library with rule of five, NIBR alerts, and PAINS.
output: Recommended filter sequence and required input column.
Suggested output fields for pass status and alert details.
Summary checks for molecule counts and filter pass rates.

output_examples.input: Prioritize a lead series for CNS-like properties.
output_examples.output: A staged plan using CNS rules, TPSA limits, complexity checks, and expert review of borderline compounds.

best_practices: Combine rules, structural alerts, and target context before removing compounds.
Keep filter decisions reproducible by saving pass rates and matched alert details.
Review known drugs, prodrugs, and natural products before applying strict exclusions.
anti_patterns: Do not treat filter failures as automatic proof that a molecule is unusable.
Do not mix unrelated target classes without documenting context-specific criteria.
Do not run large batch jobs without checking dependencies, memory, and output paths.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps apply medicinal chemistry filters, structural alerts, complexity checks, and batch compound triage workflows.

faq.question: Does it replace a medicinal chemist?
faq.answer: No. It supports screening and prioritization, but expert review remains required.

faq.question: Which molecule formats can the helper script read?
faq.answer: The script supports CSV, TSV, SDF, and plain text files with SMILES strings.

faq.question: Can it explain why compounds fail filters?
faq.answer: Yes. It can summarize failed rules, alert categories, demerits, and constraint violations when available.

faq.question: Are PAINS and structural alerts definitive?
faq.answer: No. They are screening signals that should be interpreted with assay context and chemistry judgment.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex run the batch script?
faq.answer: Yes, when the needed Python dependencies are installed and the user approves local file inputs and outputs.
